details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of damaging wind gusts and severe hail will generally remain focused across parts of northwestern Wisconsin for the next couple hours -- within Severe Thunderstorm Watch 626

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A NNE/SSW-oriented surface front/wind shift moving eastward across far northwestern WI remains the focus for ongoing convective clusters, with transient/embedded rotation. Around 30-40 kt of west-northwesterly deep-layer shear (per DLH VWP data) oriented perpendicular to the front and a narrow corridor of weak-moderate pre-convective buoyancy should continue to support this activity for the next couple hours. Given the clustered mode with some deeper/separated cores, the primary concern will continue to be damaging wind gusts and severe hail. While unlikely, the transient embedded rotation and ongoing cell interactions could still support a brief/weak tornado risk, aided by some increase in a southerly low-level jet over the next couple hours. With time and eastward extent, these storms will move into an increasingly stable air mass in north-central WI (evident in surface observations and visible satellite imagery). Therefore, a downstream watch is unlikely

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK TORNADO INTENSITY...UP TO 90 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.00-1.75 IN

details.label: Summary
details.text: Some threat exists for severe wind and hail with ongoing storms. Convective trends are being monitored for the need of a WW issuance

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Multiple multicells/supercells have matured over eastern CO over the past few hours as upslope flow of a moistened and heated airmass has encouraged relatively robust but sparse convective initiation. These storms are benefiting from 7+ C/km mid-level lapse rates and accompanying 1500-2000 J/kg MLCAPE, as well as 30 kts of effective bulk shear. Given relatively limited shear and flow, storms are expected to remain relatively sparse and slow moving. Severe wind and hail may accompany the stronger storms, but it is currently unclear how widespread severe coverage will be. Nonetheless, convective trends will continue to be monitored for the need of a Severe Thunderstorm Watch issuance
